blocks.text: Imagine you need to prove that every student in a class has passed an exam, given that each student has studied. How do you formalize and prove such statements using predicate logic?

blocks.markdown: In predicate logic, we use quantifiers to express statements about collections of objects. The two primary quantifiers are the universal quantifier (\( \forall \)) and the existential quantifier (\( \exists \)). In this lesson, we will explore how to use these quantifiers in formal proofs.

blocks.title: Universal Instantiation
blocks.text: Universal instantiation allows us to infer that a property holds for a specific individual if it holds for all individuals. Formally, from \( \forall x \, P(x) \), we can infer \( P(c) \) for any specific constant \( c \).

blocks.title: Existential Generalisation
blocks.text: Existential generalisation allows us to infer that there exists an individual with a certain property if we know a specific individual has that property. Formally, from \( P(c) \), we can infer \( \exists x \, P(x) \).

blocks.markdown: Let's see how these rules are applied in formal proofs. We will work through examples to illustrate the process of constructing a formal derivation using these rules.

blocks.title: Example of Universal Instantiation
blocks.prompt: Given the premise \( \forall x \, (P(x) \rightarrow Q(x)) \) and \( P(a) \), prove \( Q(a) \).

steps.text: Start with the premise \( \forall x \, (P(x) \rightarrow Q(x)) \).
Apply universal instantiation to obtain \( P(a) \rightarrow Q(a) \).
Use the premise \( P(a) \) and modus ponens to conclude \( Q(a) \).
Apply existential generalisation to conclude \( \exists x \, P(x) \).

blocks.markdown: When constructing formal proofs, it's crucial to apply quantifier rules correctly. Missteps can lead to invalid conclusions. Let's examine a few common pitfalls.

blocks.title: Common Mistake
blocks.text: A common mistake is to apply existential generalisation without a specific instance. Ensure you have a concrete example before generalising.

blocks.markdown: Now, let's summarize the key points from this lesson.

points: Universal instantiation allows deriving a specific case from a universal statement.
Existential generalisation allows inferring the existence of a property from a specific instance.
Correct application of these rules is essential for valid formal proofs.
